text_blocks.snippet: Sinus infections, while often manageable, can lead to serious complications if left untreated or if the infection is severe. These complications can be local, affecting the surrounding tissues, or more serious, involving the eyes or even the brain and surrounding membranes.

list.title: Orbital Cellulitis:
list.snippet: This is a common serious complication where the infection spreads from the sinuses to the tissues surrounding the eye. It can cause severe eye pain, vision problems, and even vision loss.

list.title: Preseptal Cellulitis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the eyelid and surrounding skin, often caused by the spread of infection from the sinuses.

list.title: Subperiosteal Abscess:
list.snippet: An abscess that forms between the bone and the periosteum (the membrane covering the bone) of the eye socket.

list.title: Orbital Abscess:
list.snippet: A collection of pus within the eye socket.

list.title: Dacryocystitis:
list.snippet: An infection of the tear ducts, which can occur when a sinus infection spreads towards the eyes.

list.title: Meningitis:
list.snippet: Inflammation of the membranes surrounding the brain and spinal cord, a potentially life-threatening condition that can cause severe headaches, fever, and stiff neck.

list.title: Septic Cavernous Sinus Thrombosis:
list.snippet: A blood clot in the cavernous sinus, a structure behind the eyes that can cause cranial nerve palsies (like double vision), headaches, and fever.

list.title: Osteomyelitis:
list.snippet: Infection of the bone, which can occur if the infection spreads to the bones of the skull.

list.title: Brain Abscess:
list.snippet: A collection of pus within the brain tissue, which can be life-threatening.

list.title: Reduced Sense of Smell or Taste:
list.snippet: Inflammation and blockage from the infection can impair the olfactory receptors, leading to a temporary or, in some cases, prolonged loss of smell.

list.title: Sore Throat and Cough:
list.snippet: Post-nasal drip, a common symptom of sinus infections, can irritate the throat and cause a cough.

list.title: Fatigue:
list.snippet: The body's immune response to the infection can lead to fatigue and general discomfort.

list.title: Ear Infections:
list.snippet: Sinus infections can block the eustachian tubes, leading to fluid buildup and potential middle ear infections.

list.title: Pink Eye (Conjunctivitis):
list.snippet: The inflammation and discharge from the sinuses can spread to the eyes and cause conjunctivitis.

list.title: Bad Breath:
list.snippet: Drainage from infected sinuses can mix with saliva and contribute to bad breath.
